short_answer: Danny's VIP Sports Picks is a real seller in the narrow sense that it has a live CapperTek listing, posts picks there almost daily and sells access at published prices. The seller gives no full name, company, address or website of its own that we could open, so a buyer knows very little about who is behind it.

The good news for a buyer is that a pick log exists. CapperTek records each pick with the time it was entered, the odds and the stake, and grades it. The bad news is what the log shows: on 7 Nov 2026 CapperTek put the five year window at 923 wins, 829 losses and 11 pushes, about 53% winners, for -133.00 units and a -1.60% return. The last 365 days were also negative.
Treat Danny as a small seller whose own posted record is roughly break even to losing, not as a proven winner. The cheap price is real, but a cheap pick that loses still costs you the bet.
pricing_intro: Prices below were shown on the CapperTek purchase tab for DannysVIPSportsPicks.cappertek.com on 7 Nov 2026. CapperTek says sellers set their own prices and are paid through their own PayPal account. A buyer must register a free CapperTek customer account to buy.
pricing: No refund terms shown on the listing
guarantee: We found no guarantee of any kind on the Danny's VIP listing. The bio promises how picks are delivered, not results: it says buyers get each pick at least 25 minutes before game time.

CapperTek's terms of service say that, unless otherwise stated, all fees and charges are non refundable, and that its payment portal is PayPal. Nothing on the listing states otherwise. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered by any pick seller.

claims_note: The bio says the seller figured out how to win consistently. The CapperTek log the seller keeps on the same profile does not show that. Over the windows CapperTek offers, only the shorter recent windows were positive on 7 Nov 2026 (90 days and 180 days), while the 30 day, 365 day, 730 day and five year windows were negative.

The 25 minute promise is not always kept. In the pick history, a Colorado Avalanche pick on 5 Nov 2026 was entered at 9:27 PM ET for a 9:37 PM ET start. A buyer who needs time to place a bet should know that some picks arrive close to the start.
record: Independently checkable: CapperTek, a pick marketplace that says it takes no commission on sales, keeps a documented record for this listing. Each pick shows the game, the side, the odds, the stake in units, the time the pick was made and the time it was graded, and picks are revealed to the public 30 minutes after the game starts. Its record windows read: last 30 days 44-32, -18.20 units, -3.46% ROI; last 90 days 63-45, +33.80 units, +4.88%; last 365 days 433-378-4, -59.62 units, -1.36%; last 730 days 685-567-4, -19.96 units, -0.30%; last 1,825 days 923-829-11, -133.00 units, -1.60%. CapperTek says ROI is based on a $100 per unit risk amount.

Limits of that log: the seller enters his own picks, and CapperTek is a directory and marketplace, not an auditor. We cannot see whether every pick sent to paying customers appears in it. Many picks are heavy favorites, such as Colorado at -212 and Florida at -251 in early November 2026, which is why a win rate above 50% can still lose money.

Seller marketing: the bio and reviews speak of consistent winning and a top win percentage. Those are claims; the numbers above are the log. We found no court or regulator action involving this seller in our searches, and with no legal name given there was nothing further to search.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition Danny's VIP Sports Picks is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how this handicapper performs beyond what CapperTek shows.
our_data.context: For scale: one reviewer says the NFL picks hit 80%. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even, and more when laying heavy favorites.

customers_intro: All the customer evidence we found sits on one site: seven short reviews on the seller's CapperTek page, all positive, from five usernames, one of which posted three times. We found nothing on BBB, Reddit or the betting forums. None of the reviews includes a pick log, and they do not square with the losing totals in the seller's own CapperTek record.

customers.text: One username wrote three of the seven reviews. In Feb 2024 he said Danny had won him a lot of money that weekend in hockey and basketball and called baseball Danny's strength; in Aug 2026 he said Danny was locked in on baseball with one of the higher win percentages around. The seller replied to the first with a joke about the username.

A reviewer said Danny should be ranked first because he has the best winning percentage, said the picks had made him a good amount of cash, and criticized handicappers who, in his words, pay for their top rankings. On 7 Nov 2026 the seller's own CapperTek log showed about 53% winners and a loss in units over five years.

A reviewer claimed the NFL picks hit 80% and praised the hockey and college basketball picks. He liked that Danny sends about two picks a day rather than seven and skips days with nothing he likes. He gave no sample size.

Two reviews arrived the same day. One buyer, referred by a friend and about a month in, said they could not seem to lose; the other said he only sticks with "a sure thing" and Danny had not disappointed. No bet is a sure thing, and neither review gave a record.

BBB returned no results for the name. Web searches, including site searches of Reddit, found no thread about this seller, and we found no TheRX, Covers or SBR discussion. The seller has no website of its own that loaded for us, so there was no Trustpilot or SiteJabber page to check.

conflicts: We saw no sportsbook affiliate links or promo codes on the seller's CapperTek pages. CapperTek's own footer lists Pinnacle and FanDuel as partners; that is the marketplace, not the seller.

The listing carries a CapperTek "Verified Service" label. CapperTek's FAQ says verified means the service placed a verification banner on its website and opened a line of communication so CapperTek can resolve complaints. It is not a check of results. CapperTek separately sells Pro Featured placement for a monthly advertising fee.
Reviews on CapperTek are anonymous and user submitted, and CapperTek says it does not guarantee their accuracy. A buyer cannot tell who wrote them.
strengths: A public, time stamped pick log with odds and stakes, graded by the platform, which is more than most small sellers offer.
Low prices: $10 for a day or $120 for 30 days.
Few picks a day, by the seller's and one reviewer's account, which makes the plays easier to follow and track.
concerns: The seller's own CapperTek log is negative over one, two and five years, despite a bio that claims consistent winning.
No name, company, address or website, and no refund terms beyond CapperTek's general rule that fees are non refundable.
Many plays are heavy favorites and some stakes run to 11 units, so a cold run can cost a follower a lot of money quickly.
All customer reviews come from one site, five usernames and no records.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Is Danny's VIP Sports Picks legit?

It is a real, active CapperTek seller that posts picks and sells access at published prices. The seller gives no name, company or address, and its own logged record does not show the consistent winning its bio claims.
How much does Danny's VIP Sports Picks cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 CapperTek listed $10 for 1 day, $50 for 7 days, $75 for 14 days, $120 for 30 days and $220 for 60 days. We found no refund terms, and CapperTek's terms say fees are non refundable unless stated.
Does Danny's VIP Sports Picks have a verified record?

It has a CapperTek documented record with pick times, odds and stakes, which anyone can read, though the seller enters the picks and CapperTek is not an auditor. On 7 Nov 2026 it showed 923-829-11 and -133.00 units over the last 1,825 days, and Watchdog has no graded record of its own.
Is Danny's VIP Sports Picks worth it?

For the money you get a few cheap daily picks across baseball, hockey, basketball and football. What is unproven is any long run profit: the seller's own log is down in units over one, two and five years, so a buyer would be paying for picks that have not beaten the market over time.
